correctness.rationale: For invertible matrices, strong connectivity equals algebraic simplicity even after field extension: any ideal containing a nonzero coordinate contains all squared basis vectors by path propagation; non-strong connectivity produces a terminal-component ideal. Row/column singleton zero-cut probabilities under GL_n(q) equal (q-1)/(q^n-1), and Bonferroni plus middle-cut union bounds yield 2n times this with O_q(n²q^-2n). With a loop, strong connectivity and asymmetric directed support, the known graph automorphism group-scheme exact sequence restricts to diagonal lambda_j=lambda_i², and the loop forces every lambda=1 over any test ring; hence full scheme trivial. Random graph permutation-orbit probabilities give exponential union bound. Independent 3-by-3 binary exhaustive determinant/graph check gave 168 invertibles, 80 simple, and 24 matrices with specified outward singleton cut; finite checks do not prove scheme-level claim.
